appInfoLocalization.name: Paint by Moonlight
appInfoLocalization.subtitle: Paint by numbers, your own way

versionLocalization.promotionalText: Make your own paint-by-numbers: from a photo of someone you love, by redrawing every line yourself, or printed to paint with real brushes. Made on your iPhone or iPad.
whatsNew: • Refine: redraw any painting by hand before you paint it. Draw and bend lines, split and join areas, pick every paint, or start from a blank page. The Tool Guide shows each tool on a picture to practise on.
• Five free paintings, one back each day.
• Gallery shares now show the picture in the share sheet.
description: Paint by Moonlight makes your own paint-by-numbers, three ways.

FROM A PHOTO. Choose a photo of your dog, your garden or a note in your grandmother's hand. Your iPhone or iPad draws it as a coloring book: clean lines, numbered areas and a palette of paints mixed from the photo itself, each with a name of its own, like Corn Husk or Inkpot.

BY HAND. Change the drawing yourself, as an artist would: draw lines with your finger or Apple Pencil, bend them, split and join areas, and pick each paint. Or start from a blank page and draw your own picture to paint. The Tool Guide teaches every tool with a picture to practise on.
ON PAPER. Print the template with a key to its colors, and paint it with real paints.
Then fill it in, one calm tap at a time.
MADE FROM WHAT YOU LOVE
• People and pets: the drawing closes their outlines, spends more colors and detail on them, and draws people's eyes.
• Handwriting in your photo, like a note or a card, is traced in ink and kept clear of the numbers, so a love note stays readable.

• Choose Quick, Relaxed or Detailed in Settings, and each new painting's colors, detail and smoothness are suggested to match. A painting you haven't begun can be made quicker or more detailed in place.
• Take a photo, pick one from your library, or open one from Files or another app.
CALM, SATISFYING PAINTING
• Tap an area to fill it, or touch and hold, then drag to paint along.
• On iPad, Apple Pencil paints while your fingers move around the canvas.
• Hint finds the next area of your color; Zen Mode glides there for you.
• Peek at your photo whenever you like.
• Soft sounds with every fill, and haptics on iPhone.
• Dark paper for painting at night, and three line weights.
• When you're done, replay your painting from the first fill and share it as a time-lapse.
• Turn on The Making-of in Settings to watch your photo become a painting, step by step.
A LIBRARY TO START FROM
44 public-domain pictures are built in: paintings and prints by Hokusai, Van Gogh, Vermeer, Monet, Cézanne and Hiroshige, and photographs of national parks, wildlife and the Earth from space.
SHARE IT YOUR WAY
• Print the template, with a key to its colors, and paint it with real paints.
• Send a blank copy to a friend to paint in the app, with your photo if you like.
• Save or share the finished picture.
FREE TO START
Five paintings are free, and a free one comes back each day, up to five. A one-time purchase unlocks unlimited paintings and the drawing tools. No subscription.
PRIVATE BY DESIGN

Every painting is made right on your iPhone or iPad, and your photos stay there unless you choose to share them. No account, no ads, no tracking, and it works offline. Nothing is uploaded except feedback you review and choose to send.
Built for VoiceOver, Dynamic Type and Reduce Motion, with keyboard shortcuts on iPad.

notes: No account or sign-in is needed. The app is free: five new paintings are free, and one comes back each day, up to five; every new painting takes one (a picture from The Library, a photo or a mosaic). To see the in-app purchase (Unlimited Paintings), open Settings > Unlimited Paintings, or start a sixth painting the same day; Restore Purchases is in that sheet. The purchase also unlocks the drawing tools (the pencil Change button in a painting, and Blank Page on the New Painting screen): until it is bought, they open its sheet, where Try It in the Tool Guide opens the tools' guide, whose practice pictures are free.

To try it: tap + (New Painting) and pick Tonight's Picture or a picture in The Library: the painting forms and opens by itself (tens of seconds on iPhone the first time). Paint by tapping areas whose number matches the paint selected in the palette. To draw on it, tap the pencil button (Change) beside Undo; Blank Page on the New Painting screen starts a drawing of your own. Both come with the purchase. The first launch also prepares two starter paintings in the gallery, which can take a minute.

Everything runs on the device, including the on-device models that draw the lines. The app makes no network requests except when someone taps Send in Give Feedback (the More menu on a painting): that uploads the report they reviewed to the developers.
Optional: Settings > The Making-of plays an animation of the painting being made after Start Painting. On iPad, the menu bar's Paint menu has keyboard shortcuts.

An Easter egg we want to disclose (Guideline 2.3.1): a second mode, Paint by Mosaic, in which a photo is laid as a Byzantine mosaic and set tile by tile instead of painted. It is part of the app's own code and content (nothing downloaded), works offline and collects nothing. To reach it: Settings (the gear in the gallery), About, tap the Year row, and roll the wheel that appears to its first year, 0547. To return: in its own Settings, tap the Year row (0547) and roll the wheel forward to the current year. With VoiceOver, the Year row is a button and the wheel is adjustable. Its new mosaics take the same free paintings, and the Unlimited Paintings purchase covers both modes.

com.pbordjadze.paintbynumber.unlimited.reviewNote: Open Settings > Unlimited Paintings, or start a sixth new painting on the same day, or tap the pencil button (Change) in a painting (the drawing tools come with it). The sheet has the purchase and Restore Purchases.

description: Paint by Moonlight is a new iPhone and iPad app that turns any photo into a paint-by-numbers painting, made entirely on the device, then lets you fill it in one calm tap at a time.

Its own pipeline draws each photo as a coloring book: clean outlines that close around people and pets, people's eyes drawn in, handwriting traced in ink and kept clear of the numbers, and a palette mixed from the photo itself, each paint with a name of its own. Painting is made for touch and Apple Pencil, with Zen Mode, dark paper for the evening, and a replay of the finished painting as a time-lapse; painting works with VoiceOver, area by area.

It is made by one developer, with no account, ads or tracking, and works offline. 44 public-domain pictures are built in, from Hokusai, Van Gogh and Vermeer to national parks and the Earth from space. Five paintings are free, one back each day, and a one-time purchase unlocks unlimited paintings and the drawing tools.
